nodes.lr_formula: LR+ reported directly by meta-analysis = 0.762 (95% CI 0.562-1.033). Equivalently LR+ = sens/(1-spec); pooled sensitivity of hypertension = 80.7%. The published LR+ < 1 because hypertension is nearly as common in the suspected-but-excluded control population, so its presence does NOT raise the probability of pheochromocytoma.

LR+ reported directly by meta-analysis for diaphoresis = 2.184 (95% CI 1.411-3.382); pooled sensitivity 52.4%. NOTE: the diagnostic literature quantifies 'diaphoresis/sweating' generically, not 'night sweats' specifically; no separate LR exists for nocturnal sweating, so diaphoresis is used as the closest measured proxy.

No likelihood ratio can be computed: the diagnostic literature provides NO sensitivity, specificity, LR, OR, or prevalence figure (with an N) for weight loss as a predictor of pheochromocytoma. Weight loss appears only as descriptive pathophysiology (catecholamine-driven hypermetabolism / raised resting energy expenditure). Direction is plausible (weight loss can occur) but there is no usable measured number to anchor an LR.
